text: Cardinal Virtues: Ger. Kardinaltugenden ; Fr. vertus cardinales ; Ital. virtù cardinali . The principal or leading virtues upon which the other virtues depend or 'hinge.' The term seems to have been first used by St. Ambrose, who adapted to Christian usage the Platonic classification as he found it in Cicero. The cardinal virtues are there enumerated as prudence, temperance, fortitude, and justice. Literature : ZIEGLER, Gesch. d. chr. Eth. (2nd ed.), 234 ff.; SIDGWICK, Hist. of Eth. (3rd ed.), 44, 133, 143. ( W.R.S. )
